title: Where the record refuses: the ref update, the files a check uses, journal entries committed
situation: 0128 holds the freeze where a change would be recorded: the journal's append and the project's commits. A pre-commit hook is skipped by --no-verify, cherry-pick, rebase, commit-tree with update-ref and merges, so it is not the one point every route meets. 'Anything a check uses' and a journal entry written straight into the journal's folder are left to realization.
decision: The project's history refuses at git's reference-transaction hook, which every change to a branch passes and --no-verify does not skip: a hidden harness-facing command, wired as that hook, refuses in its prepared state any branch update that brings in a commit changing a frozen example, held-out example text, frozen check, file a frozen check uses, or a journal entry superseding or retiring a frozen concept, unless the acting agent is the cut's architect; it names the cut, its architect and the paths, and the ref stays where it was. A file a frozen check uses is one its relative imports reach, transitively, that is not an output of a work package of the cut. When the ledger exists but what is frozen cannot be read, every branch update and every journal change to a concept is refused. The harness binding names the session's agent on its shell calls, so the architect's commit carries the architect; with the attempt-time gate retired, nothing else in the binding refuses a change to a file. A frozen check binds an example when it names it as <context>/<number>; a builder is not dispatched while an example its work package owns is named by no frozen check.
consequences: The freeze checks rebind to the journal and the reference-transaction hook, seen red first. This repository wires the command as its own reference-transaction hook. The attempt-time file gate leaves the binding.
